subject: Audit access playbook, pen-test window, and evidence cadence for MSA/Order Form
messages:
From: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@carecrest.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>; Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>; Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on security exhibit / pen-test window (CareCrest Order Form)

Hi Irene / team,

Thanks for the draft Order Form and MSA. Legal and Security at CareCrest reviewed the security exhibit and have a few open items we need clarified before we can sign:

- SOC 2 attestation: we need the latest report and an attestation letter confirming scoped services and data segregation.
- Pen test clause: the current language allows a broad penetration test at our discretion "with 7 days notice". We need clarification on allowed tools, a proposed test window, and a requirement that Redwood coordinate with our third-party vendor.
- Audit rights: we need to confirm whether evidence (audit logs, config snapshots) can be delivered to our external auditor and the cadence for access (quarterly vs ad-hoc).

Attached is a spreadsheet with specific evidence requests (CareCrest_Security_Questions.xlsx). Can you confirm your preferred process/timeline? We are targeting a signature by mid-December to meet our implementation schedule.

Regards,
Sarah Miller
Senior Counsel, CareCrest Health

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@carecrest.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 17:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on security exhibit / pen-test window (CareCrest Order Form)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. I copied Marcus and Laura from Legal/Compliance to triage. Quick answers and proposed path:

1) SOC 2: we will provide the SOC 2 Type II report for our inference platform (period ending 2025-12-31) and an attestation letter confirming scope and level of controls. Attached: SOC2_Attestation_Redwood_2025.pdf.

2) Pen test clause: agree that "7 days notice" is too short for a coordinated test. Proposed change: define an annual authorized pen-test window (two-week blocks) with at least 30 days' notice for full-scope tests; allow narrow-scoped scans with 72-hour notice for low-risk checks. We'll propose specific allowed tools/processes in the redline.

3) Evidence & audit access: we can deliver relevant evidence and logs to an authorized third-party auditor under an NDA. We propose an "evidence cadence" of quarterly scheduled evidence drops (document bundles) plus an ad-hoc request process for critical incidents with an SLA for delivery.

Next steps I propose: Marcus will send an internal redline to the security exhibit and pen test clause tomorrow; then we set a 30-minute legal-to-legal call this week to align on final wording. If that works, please send 3 times that suit CareCrest.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOC2_Attestation_Redwood_2025.pdf (attestation stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Miller <sarah.miller@carecrest.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Proposed redlines: pen-test, audit rights, and evidence cadence

Sarah — attaching a focused redline for the pen-test and audit paragraphs (redline_pen_test_clause.docx). Summary of our proposed changes below:

- Pen test: replace "7 days notice" with:
   • "Annual authorized testing windows: Redwood will provide two-week windows (up to two windows per year) during which CareCrest and its authorized vendors may perform approved penetration tests subject to prior written approval of test plan and tools; Redwood requires at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice for a full-scope test.
   • For low-impact vulnerability scans, a minimum of seventy-two (72) hours' notice is required; Redwood retains the right to pause scans that materially impact service availability and require immediate coordination"

- Scope & tools: require test plan submission and a list of tools; Redwood will not accept destructive testing or tools that exfiltrate production data.

- Audit rights / evidence delivery: allow delivery of discrete evidence sets (config snapshots, control evidence, redacted logs) to CareCrest's external auditor under NDA. Proposed cadence: quarterly scheduled evidence packages (within 10 business days of quarter close) and an incident-driven ad-hoc delivery SLA of 15 business days. We also propose a limited "on-site or remote auditor review" once per 12-month period subject to mutual scheduling (no direct unfettered access to production environments).

- Confidentiality & minimization: add requirements for request specificity, relevance, and data minimization; Redwood will redact PII and customer-specific content not relevant to the request.

If CareCrest agrees in principle, I'll produce a tracked redline for insertion into the security exhibit.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: redline_pen_test_clause.docx (redline stub)

Michael / Sarah — thanks, and happy to confirm next steps so we can keep to your 12/08 target: 

1) SOC 2 sharing: we can provide the SOC 2 Type II report and attestation under a mutual NDA. Earliest share: Wednesday 12/02 morning via our secure Share (link below). We will redact tester contact details and customer-specific traces as discussed.

2) Quarterly evidence delivery: Redwood supports secure delivery to an SFTP or to your auditor's secure intake. We prefer to use a pre-shared SFTP access or our secure shared drive link. For the initial quarter we will package the following: SOC 2 mapping matrix, selected control evidence, config snapshots, and redacted logs — delivery within 10 business days of quarter close.

3) Pen test windows & third-party auditors: Marcus' proposed language is acceptable in principle. Redwood can coordinate with Kane & Partners. We will provide a test-plan approval process and require 30 days' notice for full-scope tests; 72 hours for light scans. We will not accept destructive testing or any activity that exfiltrates production data.

4) Call: proposed slots (PT): 12/01 4:30–5:00pm, 12/02 9:00–9:30am, 12/03 11:00–11:30am. Please confirm one.

5) DocuSign: we will review the DocuSign envelope once legal aligns and aim to provide a final security-exhibit redline by 12/04.

I uploaded an initial audit playbook and checklist here: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/CareCrest/audit-playbook (Audit_Playbook_v1.md).

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
